ark.title: ARK check
ark.about: ARK is part of ASUS firmware. NFQWS2 may run without receiving traffic when ARK is loaded. Use the button below to check whether packets are reaching NFQWS2.
ark.model_hint: Preparation has been tested on ASUS GT-BE19000AI. ARK may also be present on other ASUS models; its presence and loading depend on firmware and its settings. Check the diagnostics below.
ark.other_model_warning: Detected {{model}}. Other models have not been tested. Use at your own risk; Frank accepts no liability for damage, data loss or connectivity loss. Backup and restore remain available on this model.
ark.explanation: Preparation backs up nine settings and turns off the enabled features in the list. After preparing or restoring, restart the router yourself from the ASUS panel.
ark.confirm_prepare: The panel will save a backup and turn off {{functions}}. Continue?
ark.confirm_restore: Restore the original values changed during preparation? Other current ASUS settings will be preserved.

readiness.runtime_unknown: All 9 ARK features are disabled, but the module state is unknown. Preparation is not confirmed. Click “Check ARK” again.

readiness.flags_unknown: {{disabled}} of 9 ARK features are confirmed disabled. Other settings are absent or unavailable; disabling all features is not confirmed. ARK module: {{runtime}}. Check again.
readiness.unavailable: No current data is available to check ARK. Preparation is not confirmed. Click “Check ARK”.

requirements.title: Getting started
requirements.intro: Start by checking the router. The check shows what is already set up.

items.platform: Platform: choose the package by Entware ABI, not just the CPU name. Root (UID 0) and working NFQUEUE are needed. An exact module profile was tested for RT-AC87U/384.13_10 and is not automatically applied to other firmware. Do not reflash merely to obtain a green status.
items.dns: SmartDNS assigns DoT/DoH to specific sites and pins IP addresses. DNS selects a service address: different CDN addresses can change a strategy’s result. Share the strategy and DNS together when the result depends on DNS. A DNS reply does not guarantee that the site works.
items.transit: Wizard path: dnsmasq stays on 53, our SmartDNS listens on 127.0.0.1:6054, with a marked postconf block for forwarding. Native local names and DHCP are kept. Restore previous DNS before stopping the runtime. Browsers and VPNs may use their own DNS.
items.ark: ARK presence: a loaded module can interfere with NFQWS2 traffic processing. “Not loaded” is favorable for the queue. Presence depends on firmware and settings. An unknown internal flag does not prove it is enabled. Do not disable absent features. If preparation is needed, back up first and reboot ASUS manually after changing settings; restore is available in the same place.
items.traffic: Choose the internet connection and testing device address. DPI Detector uses the router’s own connection, so the result on your phone can differ. VPNs and other routers in the path can also affect the test.
items.verify: On the chosen device, open the site, start a video, or place a call again. The panel’s connection check helps find the cause. Check the actual app for the result.
items.updates: Open “Update NFQWS2”, prepare the package and install it. Wait for the result. On ASUS, the panel backs up settings before replacing the package and restores the previous service state.
items.storage: Installation needs space for the package, components, and a backup. Temporary files in /tmp use RAM.
items.access: If you set a panel password, sign in before changing settings.
items.health: “Unavailable IPs” (ASUS): temporarily excludes confirmed unreachable addresses so the application can try another address. Observation requires NFQWS2 to be running. The DNS filter covers ordinary UDP DNS for selected devices; DoH, DoT and TCP DNS bypass it.
items.schedule: If the router runs low on memory, you can enable scheduled restarts. “Restart NFQWS2 after a crash” lets the service restart automatically after a crash. A manually stopped service waits for you to start it.

quick.prepare: Check router mode, Merlin and Entware in /opt. USB storage is recommended for older ASUS routers.
quick.install: Install the IPK for your architecture and open http://router-IP:90.
quick.configure: Choose the devices and a strategy. You can add a ready-made option through “Import strategies”. Then save your settings.
quick.dns: SmartDNS: choose DNS and sites → Check profile → Connect.
quick.verify: Open the required services on a selected device and test new connections.
quick.recover: For help: Share → Preview. To disconnect SmartDNS: Restore previous DNS.
quick.ark: Check the platform and packet capture. If ARK is loaded on ASUS, follow the preparation instructions.
quick.start: After changing the strategy, start or restart NFQWS2. Then open the site or app you want to use.
quick.detector: DPI Detector helps compare strategies: repeat the same test set under the same conditions before and after changes to identify DNS, TLS and QUIC issues. Errors alone do not prove DPI blocking; check actual YouTube and video playback separately on your device. Installation, help and TXT report downloads are available in the “DPI Detector” window via the button at the top of the panel.
quick.keenetic_import: The NFQWS2 Keenetic strategy converter is in Import profile → Paste Keenetic strategy. Review the result before saving.

device_profiles.title: Device profiles (optional)
device_profiles.intro: In common mode, all devices use one strategy. In per-device mode, you can assign other strategies to selected devices.
device_profiles.setup: Open Devices and add clients from the LAN list or enter an IP/MAC manually. Save the current strategy in the library, import JSON or choose a catalog entry. Create profiles and select devices: the first enabled profile from the top wins. Drag profiles or use ↑/↓ to change their order.
device_profiles.apply: Preview and Save draft do not change traffic handling. Click Apply saved mode to explicitly activate it. Start the service after applying controls whether the service should run after the operation.
device_profiles.limits: Save up to 8 strategies and create up to 16 profiles. Up to 4 additional strategies can run at a time. They require extra memory. All devices share DNS.
device_profiles.devices: The list comes from local DHCP and neighbor tables; it does not prove a client is online. MAC selection needs IP addresses found in the current LAN check; an old IP from the draft is not substituted. Refresh the list and reapply after an address changes.
device_profiles.recover: On failure, recovery attempts to restore the previous mode and service state. Check the final result; Copy reason copies the error details. To disable profiles, choose Common, save and apply. Before updating the package, apply Common mode first: automatic migration of the active mode is not guaranteed.

progress.title: Setup steps
progress.explanation: Done means the relevant configuration check passed. Partial means settings exist but still need saving, applying or connecting. Not checked means fresh data is unavailable. SmartDNS provides domain-to-DNS rules and fixed replies. Test sites separately on a selected device; a running process and DNS replies do not prove they work.

report.choose_hint: Choose a file to select the folder and JSON filename.
report.browser_hint: Your browser saves the file. To select a folder each time, enable “Ask where to save each file” in its download settings. A plain HTTP page cannot open the native folder picker itself.
report.saved_browser: The file has been handed to your browser for download.
report.help_purpose: If NFQWS2 fails or the panel cannot identify ARK, this report helps locate the failing stage: firmware and Entware, process startup, ARK, WAN and client selection, rules, queue delivery, or strategy resources.
report.help_safety: Collection only reads the current state. It does not change settings, reset counters, restart services, or reboot the router. It also works with NFQWS2 stopped, provided the web panel itself is available.
report.help_privacy: Passwords, keys, IP/MAC addresses, and the contents of your configuration, lists, and logs are excluded. The JSON stays with you and is never uploaded automatically. Share it for troubleshooting, preferably while the failure is present; it cannot recover the cause of an old outage after a reboot. Sending requires your explicit Send click after preview.

share.dpi_help_title: Why do DPI results differ from my phone?
share.dpi_help_scope: DPI Detector checks the router's own connection. The phone and router may pass through NFQWS2 differently, so a working service on the phone does not guarantee the same detector result.
share.dpi_help_clients: For a phone, computer or another LAN device, use its local IPv4 from the router's client list. If DHCP assigns the address, reserve it for the device or check the list after an address change.
share.dpi_help_address: In Only listed devices mode, add the router's WAN address to the IPv4 processing list for a normal detector run: it is the source of the router's outgoing connections. The LAN address used to open the panel is usually unsuitable. This applies to both single-router and multi-router networks.
share.dpi_help_command: Run the command above in an Entware terminal. The address after src is the source IPv4 for this route; add it to the list, with /32 if needed. Check the entry again if the WAN address changes.
share.dpi_help_all: In All devices mode, the router's own IPv4 traffic through the selected WAN is also processed; no separate address entry is needed. In All except listed devices mode, listed addresses are excluded from processing instead.
share.dpi_help_paths: The command checks the IPv4 route to 1.1.1.1. VPNs, IPv6 and policy routing may send other tests along a different path. Entering NFQWS2 does not guarantee that every test will succeed.
share.install_hint: Install the pinned DPI Detector. Older ARM uses a compatible build of the same source included in the package; other platforms download the official file. Tests run separately and network settings are preserved.

keenetic.missing_files: Pasting strategy text does not transfer the files. On Keenetic they are usually in /opt/etc/nfqws2/lua/ (Lua), /opt/etc/nfqws2/blobs/ (BIN), and /opt/etc/nfqws2/lists/ (lists); the strategy contains the exact paths. Transfer missing files from the source router into the matching directories under /opt/etc/nfqws2/ on ASUS or /etc/nfqws2/ on OpenWrt. Keep their names and contents. If a file with the same name already exists, back it up and compare its contents first. Then prepare the import again. Run Lua only from a trusted source.

openwrt.install: Install the native IPK or APK matching your OpenWrt release and exact package architecture. Panel: http://router-IP:90.
openwrt.platform: Platform: uses the native OpenWrt package manager. Match the firmware release and DISTRIB_ARCH. Requires UID 0, firewall4 and compatible NFQUEUE modules from your firmware feeds.
openwrt.storage: Memory and storage: allow space for the package, dependencies and backups. Jobs and temporary files in /tmp use RAM. Configuration is stored in /etc/nfqws2.
openwrt.transit: SmartDNS integrates through native OpenWrt facilities. Existing DHCP settings, local names and rules owned by other DNS services are preserved. Use “Restore previous DNS” to undo. A browser or VPN may use its own DNS.
openwrt.verify: Check the process, queue binding, packet delivery and a complete service response from the selected device. New connections and actual video or voice matter more than one successful HTTPS request. A VPN or another NFQWS2 on the path may affect the result.
openwrt.updates: Updates: Prepare package → Install update. Active settings and the selected service state are preserved; wait for the final status. The first installation creates a configuration with processing disabled.
openwrt.auth_required: Set a root password in the OpenWrt administration panel, then reload this page. If a separate panel password is already configured, check its authorization file at /etc/nfqws2-web/auth.json.

mtproto.title: Install or update Telegram proxy
mtproto.intro: Choose where to run your Telegram proxy. The device needs internet access and Python 3 or Docker.
mtproto.help_entware: For ASUS routers with Entware. Choose an unused TCP port of 1024 or higher. The proxy runs separately from NFQWS2.
mtproto.help_linux: For Linux with systemd, Python 3 and python3-venv. The proxy runs as a separate service.
mtproto.help_docker: For Docker on x86-64 or ARM64. Install through Portainer or the terminal.
mtproto.invalid_server: Enter an IP or hostname without https://, path or port.
mtproto.port_help: Choose a free port, 1–65535. The installer does not open firewall ports.
mtproto.high_port: Without Docker, choose a port from 1024 to 65535.
mtproto.random_failed: Secure random generation is unavailable in this browser. Use a current browser.
mtproto.step_install: 1. Install or update on the selected device
mtproto.run_entware: Copy the entire command into PuTTY or SSH on the ASUS and run it. It starts a separate nfqws-mtproto service.
mtproto.run_linux: Copy the entire command into a root shell (sudo -i) on the Linux device and run it.
mtproto.run_docker: Copy the entire command into a shell on the Docker host and run it. Our previous nfqws-mtproto installation will be updated.
mtproto.connect_help: After a successful installation, open the link on your Telegram device. A running service alone does not confirm that Telegram works: check messages and media.
mtproto.private: The link contains the proxy secret. Copy it before closing this window and share it only with people you want to grant access to.
mtproto.update_help: Updating keeps the installed proxy’s port, secret and previous running or stopped state. Use your existing link or the one printed after verification. The installer restores the previous version if the update fails to start.
mtproto.portainer_update_help: To update in Portainer, open the existing stack, replace only image with the image below, and select Update the stack. Keep the existing PROXY_SECRET, port and other settings; the connection link stays the same. Choose “Install” for a new setup.
mtproto.image_for_update: Image for updating an existing stack
mtproto.copy_failed: Copy failed. Select and copy the text manually.
mtproto.run_portainer: In Portainer, open Stacks → Add stack and name it nfqws-mtproto. Paste the configuration into Web editor and select Deploy the stack. Choose a free port; keep any existing proxy.
mtproto.server_help_entware: At home, Telegram uses this ASUS router’s IP. You can change the address.
mtproto.server_help_docker: The AI Board address is filled in when detected. For Docker on another computer or NAS, enter its IP.
mtproto.server_help_linux: Enter the IP of the Linux server where you will install the proxy.
mtproto.server_remote_help: To use Telegram away from home, enter your public IP or DDNS name. Configure access to the chosen TCP port on your router.
mtproto.address_detected: Address filled in automatically. You can edit it.
mtproto.owned_only: This panel can update or remove a proxy installed here or with its installer command.
mtproto.remove_help: Run this command on the device hosting the proxy. It stops our service and removes it from startup, retaining its settings and a stopped backup.
mtproto.portainer_remove: In Portainer open our nfqws-mtproto stack and select Remove. Remove only that stack. Save its settings and keep data volumes.

ip_health.title: Unavailable IPs
ip_health.intro: The router temporarily skips addresses confirmed as unavailable, so it can try another address sooner.
ip_health.toggle_help: When a service has multiple addresses, the router can try another one sooner.
ip_health.disabled_note: Exclusion is off. Saved entries and incident history are preserved.
ip_health.auto_help: Each address is checked at most once every 15 minutes. Three successful checks put it back in use.
ip_health.evidence_note: One failure or timeout does not add an address to the list.
ip_health.dns_available: Filters plain UDP DNS requests for the selected connection and devices.
ip_health.dns_limit: Encrypted DNS (DoH and DoT) and DNS over TCP do not use this list.
ip_health.empty_help: An address appears once repeated checks confirm it is unavailable.
ip_health.clear_help: Remove all current entries. Addresses can return after a new independent confirmation. Incident history is preserved.
ip_health.last_known: The panel is showing the most recent status it received.
ip_health.list_note: “Recheck” queues the address. It goes back into use after three successful checks.

runtime.socket_unavailable: The router cannot run separate address checks. Monitoring is unavailable.
runtime.socket_preparing: Preparing address checks. Your NFQWS2 settings are preserved.
runtime.socket_setup_failed: Could not prepare address checks. Your NFQWS2 settings are preserved.
runtime.multiwan_unsupported: Monitoring is unavailable with multiple uplinks.
runtime.queue_in_use: Checks are unavailable while another service uses the network queue.
runtime.clock_unavailable: Set the router clock to enable monitoring.

errors.request_failed: Could not load IP status. Check the connection and refresh.
errors.timeout: The router did not reply in time. Refresh status to try again.
errors.invalid_response: The panel received incomplete data. Select “Refresh status”.
errors.unauthorized: Sign in to the panel again to load IP status.
errors.forbidden: Refresh the session, then repeat the action you need. Actions are never retried automatically.
errors.stale_revision: The list changed. Current status has been reloaded; review it before repeating the action.
errors.action_unknown: The action result could not be confirmed. Status has been requested again; the action was not repeated.

dpi_terminal.title: DPI Detector
dpi_terminal.description: Check DNS, sites and connections from the router. Use the keyboard or the on-screen buttons. Closing the window stops the terminal and its check.
dpi_terminal.key_save: S: save the original TXT report on the router
dpi_terminal.saved_hint: Scroll the report with the mouse wheel or a swipe. To download it, press S to save, then refresh “TXT reports” below.
dpi_terminal.unavailable: The terminal could not open. Check whether DPI Detector is installed on the router.
dpi_terminal.unsupported_abi: A compatible version of DPI Detector is not yet available for this router.
dpi_terminal.session_error: Your panel session expired. Sign in and open DPI Detector again.
dpi_terminal.busy: DPI Detector is already in use by another terminal or check. Close it or wait for it to finish, then reopen this window.
dpi_terminal.input_limit: That input is too large. Type or paste a smaller amount.
dpi_terminal.install_failed: DPI Detector installation did not finish. Refresh its status and retry installation if needed.
dpi_terminal.request_failed: The terminal connection failed. Close this window and reopen DPI Detector to try again.
dpi_terminal.state_expired: The terminal session expired. Close this window and reopen DPI Detector.
dpi_terminal.state_output_limit: DPI Detector stopped because the report reached the size limit.
dpi_terminal.state_failed: The check could not continue. The terminal stopped.
dpi_terminal.remove_confirm: Uninstall the installed DPI Detector? Its current terminal and tests will stop.
dpi_terminal.remove_keep_reports: Detector will be removed. Saved reports will be kept.
dpi_terminal.remove_with_reports: Detector and saved reports will be deleted. Reports cannot be restored from the panel.
dpi_terminal.reports_not_removed: Not all reports could be deleted. Detector is still installed. Refresh the report list before trying again.
dpi_terminal.guide_title: How to use it and read the results
dpi_terminal.guide_purpose: The checks help locate a problem in DNS, connecting to a site, or transferring data. They run from the router.
dpi_terminal.guide_install: Select “Install DPI Detector” if prompted. The check menu opens after installation.
dpi_terminal.guide_run: Start with checks 1, 2 and 3. Use the arrow keys and Space to select them, then press Enter. On phones, use the buttons below the screen.
dpi_terminal.guide_compare: Save a report with NFQWS2 off, then turn it on and repeat the same checks. Change one setting at a time when comparing results.
dpi_terminal.guide_results: If DNS fails, check the DNS settings first. If a connection does not open, check the address. Compare strategies when data transfer fails. One failure can have several causes.
dpi_terminal.guide_save: Press S in the results menu. Under “TXT reports”, select “Refresh list” and download the report you need.
dpi_terminal.reports_hint: Press S in the results menu to save the original TXT on the router. Then refresh this list and click “Download TXT” beside the report you need to save it to your device.
dpi_terminal.reports_empty: No saved reports yet. After a test, press S in the results menu and refresh this list.
dpi_terminal.report_delete_failed: Could not delete the report. Refresh the list and try again.
dpi_terminal.report_changed: The report changed or failed its integrity check. Refresh the list.
dpi_terminal.reports_failed: Could not load or download the reports. Refresh the list and try again.
dpi_terminal.result_scope: “OK” means the server replied, even with an error. Open the site or app on your device to check it yourself.
dpi_terminal.native_context: The original TXT report does not record the NFQWS2 settings used for the check.
dpi_terminal.guide_scope: “Service checks” shows the replies to three test requests, including response codes and NFQWS2 state before and after each request. Check sign-in, video and voice in the app itself.

dpi_site_check.title: Service checks
dpi_site_check.incomplete: The router tests replies from three addresses. Check sign-in, video and calls in the app itself.
dpi_site_check.dns_scope: Your DNS choice applies only to this check.
dpi_site_check.switch_hint: Switching here closes the DPI Detector terminal. Wait a moment if the check is temporarily unavailable.
dpi_site_check.http_error: HTTP error response from the server
dpi_site_check.redirect_response: Server redirects to a different address
dpi_site_check.read_limited: Part of the response was read
dpi_site_check.outcome_timeout: Server did not respond in time
dpi_site_check.outcome_blocked_address: The router skipped a non-public address
dpi_site_check.busy: Detector is busy or the terminal is still closing. Wait briefly, then run the check again.
dpi_site_check.invalid_response: The panel received incomplete or outdated data. Run the check again.
dpi_site_check.request_failed: The check request failed. Retry when the panel connection is available.
dpi_site_check.download_failed: Could not start the TXT download. Try again.
dpi_site_check.snapshot_scope: Router state is checked before and after each request.
dpi_site_check.clock_changed: The router clock changed during the check. Request duration was measured separately.
dpi_site_check.dns_local_resolver: Requests use the router’s local DNS. The router can forward them to SmartDNS when connected.
dpi_site_check.dns_system_resolver: Requests use the router’s system DNS. It may use a different server from SmartDNS.
dpi_site_check.dns_failed: DNS returned no address; TLS and HTTP were not tested
dpi_site_check.endpoint_response: A test address replied. Check the page, video or call you need in the app.
dpi_site_check.custom_scope: The router checks the HTTPS reply, ping and route for each address.
dpi_site_check.custom_hint: Enter up to 10 public IPv4 addresses or hostnames, one per line. For example, example.com or 8.8.8.8.
dpi_site_check.custom_invalid: Enter up to 10 distinct public IPv4 addresses or domains, one per line.
dpi_site_check.network_hint: The router traces up to 12 hops. An asterisk means that hop did not answer the probe.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_limit: A single check may leave the cause of a failure uncertain.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_dns_non_public: DNS returned a non-public address. The router skipped connecting to it.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_dns_nxdomain: DNS could not find the name (NXDOMAIN). Check the address and DNS settings.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_dns_error: DNS returned an error code. The cause and source of any restriction are unknown.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_dns_failed: DNS returned no IPv4 address. Check the site name and the selected DNS.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_http_451: HTTP 451 reports a legal access restriction.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_http_403: The server refused the request (HTTP 403). This reply alone does not identify why.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_http_received: An HTTP response was received. Page content and the presence of a block page have not been checked.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_ip_tls: The secure connection by IP could not be verified. Try the hostname, which the server may require.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_tls: The certificate could not be verified or the secure connection could not open. The cause is unknown.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_timeout: The server did not reply in time. Check whether the problem repeats.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_connection: Connection or transfer failed. The cause and source of any restriction are unknown.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_route_only: Ping and traceroute replies are shown. They do not establish the cause of an HTTPS restriction.
dpi_site_check.diagnosis_unknown: Insufficient evidence to determine a restriction type.
